_help.about: How old the world's plants are when you find them (design: the planet is at the tribal stage, so nothing has ever been logged, cleared or farmed — every forest is OLD GROWTH: a stand dominated by big old trees at the top of their species' size, with a scatter of giants, a thin cohort of young trees in the gaps, and standing snags). Read by VegetationPlacer when a chunk grows its trees. Restart after editing.
_help.mode: old_growth (the tribal planet) or even (the older uniform roll, for comparison).
_help.old_share: The share of emergent and canopy trees that are old: their height rolls in the top part of the species' height_m band (old_min .. 1 of the band, biased to the top by old_pow: lower = more of them at the very top).
_help.young_share: The rest: the regeneration cohort in gaps and under the crowns, rolled between young_min and young_max of the band. old_share + young_share should be 1.
_help.giant_chance: Chance an emergent tree is a giant, taller than its band (x giant_scale). Old growth: about one in four emergents.
_help.growth_floor: Trees are placed at least this far through their life (0-1, PlantMeshes.stand_in_growth): full crowns everywhere, thinning a little on the oldest.
_help.shrub_pow: Shrubs and ground plants: exponent on the roll across their band (1 = even; below 1 favours big).
